summary: Duke–Schulze-Pillot needs one fixed ternary form and n varying. The only ternary forms the repo attaches to ES are the Gross lattices of Λ_{d,m} (QUATERNION_ES Lemma 1.2), and for those representation of p is trivial (Z2741: the binary subform of Λ_{1,1} represents every p ≡ 1 mod 3). The chain lattice of a word is a different form for each word: its Gram matrix [[−v,1,0],[1,−t,1],[0,1,−u]] is negative definite of determinant −p, so the form changes with p and DSP's fixed-form theorem does not apply to a single ES problem.
not_done: No Duke–Schulze-Pillot effective/ineffective check was run; the citation (Duke–Schulze-Pillot, Ann. Math. 1990: large represented n ineffective) is from memory, not verified here.
next: None unless a ternary form whose representation of p would be an ES certificate is written down.

summary: Kronecker–Hurwitz identity Σ_s H(4N−s²) = 2σ(N) − Σ_{d|N} min(d,N/d) checked for small N (sanity). Tested M_t^lev(n) = (τ(N)−σ_{χ_{−t}}(N))/φ(t), N = tn+1 (FRONTIER §2.3 normalisation), against Hurwitz sums Σ_{t≤20} Σ_s H(4tn−s²) over 2 ≤ n ≤ 300: no exact linear relation (least-squares residual ≈ 20 on values ~10, slope ≈ 0). Per-t regressions of τ(N)−σ_χ(N) on 2σ(N)−λ(N) at N = tn+1 for t = 3, 4, 8 give residuals ≈ 11–13. The two sides involve divisors of tn+1 versus of 4tn−s², so no identity of this shape exists in the tested range.
not_done: Did not test the sums over s restricted to Type-I/II-compatible s, nor n ≥ 300, nor the weighted (χ-twisted) Hurwitz analogues.
next: None unless a precise target sum over s is written down.

summary: Calibrated the box of COMPOSITION_ES §2 for odd n ≤ 61 and μ ∈ (√n, √n + 40] (f = μ² − n, O' = ℤ[2√f], h⁺ = 2h(16f) by Prop 1.2(c), box size ∏(2v_ℓ(μ)+1) over S(μ)) (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_box.py). The box is smaller than h⁺ for 90% of the 1120 pairs (median ratio 0.25), so pigeonhole in Cl⁺ over the box cannot force the δ-fibre for most μ. The count of D | μ realised with A ≤ 400 is a lower bound only (1.4%), since the orbits are unbounded.

summary: Derived and checked (exact quaternion arithmetic, scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_gross.py) that the trace-zero lattice of Λ_{d,m} is Zu+Zv+Z(2uv−1) with norm form d b² − bc + m c² + (4dm−1) k², i.e. the binary form of discriminant 1−4dm plus ⟨4dm−1⟩. For all primes p ≡ 1 (24), p ≤ 10⁴, and d,m ≤ 20, every such p is represented by some Gross form; (1,1) alone already represents all 143 of them, because its binary part x²−xy+y² has class number one (p = x²−xy+y² iff p ≡ 1 mod 3). So the representability of p by these ternary lattices is automatic and carries no ES information; the ES condition in QUATERNION_ES Prop 2.1 is p | 4dm−1 (a divisibility), not representation of p.
not_done: Genus/class-number and spinor-genus enumeration of the Gross lattices (needs a ternary genus enumerator, not written); the Eichler-order class numbers of Z3074 were not computed.

summary: For γ = [[t,−A*],[A,−p]] ∈ SL₂(ℤ) (c = A > 0, = −γ_w^{-1}), computed Rademacher's Φ(γ) = (t−p)/A − 12 s(−p,A) exactly for all 118 words of primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 300. Φ mod 2 (equivalently 12Φ mod 24) takes both parities for both signs (sign −1: 28 even / 54 odd; sign +1: 18 / 18), so Φ does not determine (A/p). The quadratic part of the multiplier is the Jacobi symbol (p/A) = (A/p) (checked: 85/85 odd-A words), which is just Jacobi reciprocity and is not captured by Φ mod 2 (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_rademacher.py).
not_done: Did not evaluate the full eta multiplier ν(γ) (a 24th root) with the standard sign convention; only the Rademacher Φ and the Jacobi symbol were compared; Rademacher symbol for the conjugacy-invariant version not tested.
next: Evaluate ν(γ) exactly and compare with (A/p) if a convention check is wanted; the sign is already the Jacobi symbol (p/A) for odd A.

summary: Category check: a word (A,A*) with AA* = tp+1 is an arithmetic datum (a factorisation of N = tp+1 with congruences A ≡ A* ≡ −1 mod t), not a point of X(1)×X(1); its count is the divisor count D_t^−(tp+1) of FRONTIER §2.3, which I did not re-verify. Hirzebruch–Zagier cycles and their intersection numbers are attached to discriminants of quadratic fields, and a pair with AA* = N is not a CM point or intersection point without an extra embedding datum. The item's 'check' therefore has no object to test; I record the category mismatch rather than a Hecke computation.
not_done: No CM/intersection computation; no literature check of the Hirzebruch–Zagier intersection formula.
next: None unless the item is restated with a specific embedding of (A,A*) into a quaternion or Hilbert-modular datum.

summary: Since AA* = tp + 1 = N exactly (not just mod p), the word-pairing A ↦ A* = N/A is the Atkin–Lehner-type involution on the divisors of N, and (A*/p) = (A/p) for every word (A* ≡ A^{−1} mod p because AA* ≡ 1 mod p). Checked on all 2554 words of primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000: AA* = tp+1 holds in every case and sign(A*) = sign(A) in every case (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_ALsign.py). So the ES sign is invariant under the involution that a level-N moduli interpretation would give, and no extra constraint on the sign comes from the Atkin–Lehner sign. A genuine X₀(N)-cover identification was not attempted.
not_done: No explicit cover of X0(N_t) and no Galois/Atkin–Lehner sign computation; the 'bijection with points' was not written down.
next: None; the sign-invariance under A ↦ A* is a one-line identity.

summary: Took the item's orbit test literally on the F_p side: for all 101 primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000, L3(p) = {tu−1 : word} is closed under A ↦ A^{-1} (=A*), never under A ↦ −A (0/101), and has trivial multiplicative stabiliser {s ∈ F_p^*: sL3 = L3} = {1} (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_qrorbit.py). So the only symmetry of S₃(p) is the order-2 inversion, whose orbits are the pairs {A, A*}, and no subgroup of QR-stabilising symmetries forces or forbids S₃ ⊆ QR.
not_done: Did not test the full PSL₂(F_p) acting on P¹(F_p) (no natural action on F_p^* preserving QR was found beyond the multiplicative and inversion maps); did not test p ≡ 5 (8).
next: None from this item unless a PSL₂ action on the words (not on F_p) is identified.

summary: Fourier transform of 1_{L3(p)} on F_p computed exactly for the 161 primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 5000 (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_fourier.py): f̂(ξ) has no zero at any ξ ≠ 0, so Tao's uncertainty bound |supp f| + |supp f̂| ≥ p+1 is satisfied with huge slack and gives no constraint. The quadratic coefficient Σ_{A∈L3}(A/p)/|L3| is at most 0.53 for these primes; over all primes p ≡ 1 (8), 17 ≤ p ≤ 10⁶ (full sweep, data/z52b/pass2/NC3/words_1e6.txt) its maximum is 0.80 (p = 21841), and #QNR in L3 is ≥ 2 everywhere (minimum at p = 17) with no prime of this class having L3 ⊆ QR. The 'S3 ⊆ QR' failure needs ratio 1.
not_done: Only p ≤ 5000; the uncertainty route was not pushed to the full S_L(p) union (L ≥ 4) and no bound on the quadratic coefficient is proved.
next: None for this item; the observed bias (ratio ≤ 0.53) is the quantity any Fourier argument would need to beat.

summary: The item's determinant is the continuant: tuv − u − v = det of the tridiagonal matrix with diagonal (v,t,u) and off-diagonal −1 (checked by hand). The LGV/matching expansion of a path with loops (v,t,u) is Σ over matchings of (−1)^{|M|} ∏(unmatched loop weights), which has the same signs as the continuant (e.g. tuv − v − u). So any LGV network for M(t,u,v) has signed, not positive, path weights; positivity is not obtained, and A = tu−1 = the 2-matching sum of (t,u). No count was computed beyond this identity.
not_done: No explicit planar network with non-negative weights was attempted; the parity/4-divisibility interpretation was not tested.
next: None: the natural network is signed.

summary: Built X_p = flag complex on the words of p with edges between words sharing a coordinate value, σ(t,u,v) = (t,v,u) (A ↦ A*). For p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 120, X_p is F_2-acyclic (all reduced Betti numbers 0), and σ has no fixed vertex (u = v is impossible for prime p). Smith's theorem is then satisfied only by σ-invariant edges {(t,u,v),(t,v,u)} (these always exist, as the two words share t), so the forced fixed point is a trivial midpoint and carries no certificate information (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_topo.py).
not_done: Did not use the 'near-solution' complex or p > 120; complex choice (share-a-letter flag complex) is mine, the item left it open.
next: None; a useful Smith argument needs an involution with fixed points that are not forced by the t-coordinate.

summary: Poset = L3(p) under divisibility of the A-values; Euler characteristic of its order complex (sum over chains) computed for all 101 primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000 (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_poset.py). The values χ range over 0–20 with no pattern and are not equal to |L3(p)| in 97 cases (divisibility chains are common), and χ = 0 occurs once. A nonzero χ gives no existence statement about certificates since the poset is defined from the certificates themselves.
not_done: Did not construct a Forman matching or discrete Morse function; the poset of 'divisor pairs' with a different order was not tested.
next: None; Euler characteristic of this poset does not track the sign (A/p).

Tested the item's 'small class-group exponent' hypothesis on h-type data: exp Cl(−4n) ≤ 2 holds for 30% of failures vs 12% of representable n in the size-matched window n ≤ 300 (80 vs 218 values), and for only 25/111 failures ≤ 2·10⁵ (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_i3class.py). The property is neither necessary nor characteristic, so no Siegel-type finiteness mechanism is indicated by these data.

summary: The 3-chain sign is a function of (t,u,v) mod 4 and p mod 8 (0 conflicts for p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000; this is the PROVED slot lemma, FOREST_CONNECTIVITY Thm 2.1). For 4-chains (a,b,c,d) with continuant p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000, and cofactor A = K(b,c,d), the sign (A/p) is also a function of (a,b,c,d) mod 4 (6250 chains, 90 residue classes, 0 conflicts), while the naive rules ('4 | entry' or '4 | sub-continuant') match only 1348/1730 and 1216/1730 chains. The likely mechanism is the Barkan–Hickerson–Knuth formula (Jacobi symbol = sign of an alternating sum of partial quotients mod 4; Girstmair arXiv:1501.00655, Tsukerman arXiv:1501.03544), which would give an exact mod-4 rule for all chain lengths.
not_done: No σ − w² mod 8 (Gauss–Milgram) computation; the sign rule was tested, not derived; no 5-chain run; the explicit BHK rule for 4-chains was not written down.
next: Derive the exact mod-4 rule for L-chains from the Girstmair/BHK alternating-sum congruence and check it on the 4-chain table.

summary: Morier-Genoud–Ovsienko q-rational [A-regular-CF of p/A]_q (sanity q→1 OK) evaluated at q = e^{iπ/4} for all 118 words of primes p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 300: 36 distinct phases; the phase-to-sign majority rule is 96.6% correct against a 69% baseline (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_mgo.py). The phase is not a function of (t,u,v) mod 4 (18 of 20 classes conflict), so this is not just the slot-lemma mod-4 pattern. At q = i, the phase takes 3 values shared by both signs, and 55 evaluations hit a pole (a partial quotient ≡ 0 mod 4 gives [a]_q = 0). The 3.4% of misclassified words are the test of whether this is an exact invariant.
not_done: Only p ≤ 300; no check of other roots of unity (order 8 only); no check whether the phase is a function of CF length or of the parity of the regular CF; not compared with HJ data.
next: Test whether the phase at ζ_8 is an exact function of a CF statistic (length parity, number of entries ≡ 1 mod 4) on p ≤ 10⁴; if the 96.6% does not become exact, record it as an artefact of the CF structure.

summary: Took the resistance of a word to be R = A/p (the series–parallel CF-network value, unit resistors) and ordered the words of each prime p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000 by R. Along this order the Legendre sign changes 939 times against a fully random order mean of 996 (99 primes; scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_fan.py). No monotone sign pattern, so Rayleigh-monotonicity gives no ordering of the sign; the 6% deficit of changes is a weak clustering and not a structure.
not_done: The fan graph itself was not built (its conductances were not given); R = A/p is the CF-network value, not a Kirchhoff computation on the fan. No Rayleigh-monotone chain was tested beyond this single ordering.

summary: The Hilbert basis of the cone of 1/p(1,A) has r(p/A)+2 elements (the classical Riemenschneider/Oda fact, quoted from memory, not re-derived here), so 'five elements' is exactly r(p/A)=3, i.e. A ∈ L3(p). Among the words of p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 3000, the r=3 cones take both Legendre signs (e.g. p=13: two QR and two QNR values; totals per prime in data/z52b/pass2/NC3/words_1e6.txt), so the Hilbert-basis size does not determine the sign. The class group of the toric ring is Z/p for every A, and the isomorphism class depends on A only through {A, A^{-1}}, which does not separate QR from QNR.
evidence: DEDEKIND_ES.md §1 (HJ length = number of Hilbert-basis elements minus 2, implicit)
not_done: No Macaulay2/Normaliz Hilbert series or a-invariant (not installed); the Hilbert-basis size was not recomputed by brute force, only the classical count was used.
next: None unless a ring invariant beyond the Hilbert basis size is proposed.

summary: Defined Λ_q(S) = {x ∈ ℤ^k : ∏ s_i^{x_i} ≡ 1 (mod q)} for S = first k primes not dividing q (k = 3, 5, 8), q prime 50 ≤ q ≤ 3000, via discrete logarithms; computed exact λ₁ (PARI qfminim on an LLL-reduced basis) and compared with the Gaussian heuristic GH = √(k/2πe)·det^{1/k}. The relation lattices have systematically longer shortest vectors than GH predicts at small k: short relations (certificate-like) are rarer than a random-lattice model says.

summary: The proved transport statements in TRANSPORT_LAW.md (the Ptolemy law, §1) and DELTA_TRANSPORT.md (folding moves) act on windows or words, not on integers n ↦ f(n). The only self-map of ℕ among the proved facts is ES(n) ⇒ ES(kn), so the generated semigroup is {n ↦ kn} and its orbits on primes are {kp}; the failure set is then downward closed under divisibility, as the item says. Since ES holds for all n ≤ 3000 by the Lean kernel check of Z2886 and for n ≤ 10^17 by FRONTIER §1, the failure set is empty in that range and the orbit statement is vacuous there.

summary: Verified the 4-chain Euler–Minding identity K(a,b,c,d)·K(b,c) − K(a,b,c)·K(b,c,d) = −1 for all 10⁴ quadruples with entries in 2..11 (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_misc1.py). So K(a,b,c)·K(b,c,d) = p·K(b,c) + 1 is the length-4 analogue of AA* = tp+1, with A = K(b,c,d) and A' = K(b,c) = p⁻¹ mod A up to sign. The sign of the 4-chain is governed by the mod-4 rule of Z2782, so this identity adds no new constraint.

summary: H_t(q) = Σ_n σ_{χ_{−t}}(tn+1) q^{tn+1}. For t = 4 and t = 8, H_t² lies exactly in M_2(Γ₀(t²)) (dim 5 and 14).
